title: AgentSight conversation import file (v1)
description: The format for bulk-importing historical conversations and messages into AgentSight. Only fields that map 1:1 onto a storable column are accepted; unknown keys are an error rather than being ignored, so a typo like 'converstaion_id' fails loudly instead of silently dropping the value.
$comment: Three contract rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced only by the backend (data_imports/validation.py): metadata nesting depth (max 10), metadata serialized size (max 16 KB), and each message timestamp being at or after its conversation's started_at. Passing this schema is necessary, never sufficient. Client-side validation against this file is a UX nicety; the backend is the authority.

schema_version.description: Must be exactly 1. Bumped only for a breaking format change; a file declaring an unknown version is rejected rather than guessed at.

conversations.description: Every conversation in the file. conversation_id must be unique across the whole array, and must not already exist for this agent.

conversation.title: Conversation
conversation.$comment: Also the per-record subschema the backend validates each staged conversation against, so chunk validation and whole-file validation cannot diverge.

conversation_id.description: Your system's identifier for the conversation. Unique within the file, and the key AgentSight deduplicates on — re-uploading a file whose ids already exist is rejected, never silently merged.
conversation_id.$comment: The pattern requires at least one non-whitespace character and forbids NUL anywhere. Postgres rejects NUL in TEXT and JSONB, so an unchecked NUL would pass validation and then blow up mid-commit as an opaque 500.

started_at.description: When the conversation began. ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset or Z — a timestamp with no offset is ambiguous and would land the conversation in the wrong analytics bucket.

customer_id.description: Your identifier for the end user, used to group conversations by customer.

language.description: Free-form language marker, e.g. 'en'. Stored verbatim, not validated against a language list.

device.description: Free-form device or channel marker, e.g. 'web', 'ios'.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON object of your own fields, shown in the dashboard and filterable.

messages.description: The transcript. At least one message is required — a conversation with none is source noise, and duration analytics need at least one message timestamp. Order does not matter; messages are sorted by timestamp on import.

sender.description: Who sent the message. Case-insensitive, surrounding whitespace ignored. Anything outside the alias map below — 'system', 'tool', 'function' — is an error: AgentSight stores a two-sided transcript and has no honest place to put those, so strip them before uploading.
sender.$comment: A case-insensitive pattern rather than an enum on purpose. JSON Schema enums are case-sensitive, so an enum would reject 'User' here while the backend accepts it — making client-side pre-validation stricter than the server, which is the worst failure mode for a migration tool.

content.description: The message text, stored exactly as given. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character.
content.$comment: Content is NOT sanitized on import — the live ingestion path stores raw text too, and render-time escaping is the frontend's job. Do not assume an imported transcript has been cleaned.

timestamp.description: When the message was sent. ISO 8601 with an explicit offset or Z, and at or after the conversation's started_at (that comparison is checked by the backend, not by this schema).

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON object of your own fields for this message, e.g. the model that produced it.

timestamp.$comment: The trailing group is mandatory: that is what enforces 'explicit offset or Z'. The pattern, not 'format', does the work — JSON Schema validators skip format assertions by default, and 'date-time' would accept a naive timestamp anyway. Shaped to match what django.utils.dateparse.parse_datetime accepts, so this schema never rejects a value the backend would take. The backend additionally rejects timestamps before 2000-01-01 or more than 5 minutes in the future.

optionalText.$comment: Optional fields accept an explicit null as well as being absent, because real exporters emit nulls for empty columns. Required fields never accept null.

metadataObject.$comment: Recursive, so the key-count and key-name rules apply at every level rather than only the top one. The forbidden key names are a prototype-pollution guard: harmless in Postgres, dangerous the moment stored JSON is spread into an object by a JS consumer, and the dashboard renders metadata. Nesting depth (max 10) and serialized size (max 16 KB) are NOT checked here — JSON Schema cannot express either.
